segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: Hey Jordan, quick one on Northline Parts. I’m cleaning up the forecast for April and the account is still sitting in commit for 62 seats, $31,800 annual.

segments.speaker: Jordan
segments.text: Yeah, I saw that. They added the warehouse team in January, right? Ten extra viewer seats and two admin seats.

segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: Correct. Billing tool shows the prorated invoice paid on January 18, so no issue there. The only thing is their current agreement ends March 31, and I don’t see any call notes or emails where we’ve talked to them about continuing.

segments.speaker: Jordan
segments.text: Okay. That’s not ideal, but fixable. Who’s the day-to-day over there now, still Priya in operations?

segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: Yeah, Priya Singh. She was on the implementation wrap call. Their go-live for the Dallas site is April 15, and support has two open tickets, both pretty normal configuration stuff.

segments.speaker: Jordan
segments.text: Got it. I’d keep the renewal simple then. Same 62 seats, same terms, maybe a 3% uplift if the pricing sheet supports it.

segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: It does. That puts them at $32,754 for twelve months. Net 30, auto-renewal language stays the same unless legal asks for changes.

segments.speaker: Jordan
segments.text: Can you send Priya a short note today and ask for a 20-minute check-in? Don’t make it a big procurement thing yet.

segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: Yep. I’ll also update the CRM close date to April 5 and move it to best case until we hear back.

segments.speaker: Jordan
segments.text: Perfect. If she mentions needing a PO, loop in deal desk early. Their last PO took, what, nine business days?

segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: Eight, I think. I’ll attach the prior invoice and the seat summary so they’re not hunting for it.
